raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
> Part of the HiCache MLA host-dedup series — this final PR also carries the series umbrella (see **Series overview** below). This is `[8/N]`, stacked on `[7/N]` (#45176). Depends on `[3/N]` (#45141 — base shared-CPU read), `[5/N]` (#45173 — V4 multi-pool), and `[6/N]` (#45175 — Kimi hybrid).
>
> **Validation gate:** like `[3/N]` (#45141), this extension was hand-ported onto the post-#43595 pool-construction architecture (including the `MambaPoolHost` buffer-info signature). Before merging, run the shared-read UTs listed under Accuracy Tests on real hardware.

## Series overview

This is the final PR of an **opt-in** host-side deduplication series for MLA/DSA HiCache pools. Under plain tensor parallelism, MLA/DSA KV is **identical across attention-TP ranks**, yet HiCache stores a separate CPU (L2) copy per rank — wasting host memory and, with the `file` L3 backend, making every rank re-read the same bytes. The series keeps a single physical CPU copy of the replicated KV/indexer and restores it either by (a) owner-read-then-broadcast, or (b) all ranks reading the same shared CPU mapping directly. Rank-private Mamba/KDA state and independent draft shards stay per rank; replicated V4 compression-state regions are included in this shared-read extension. Dedup is **off by default**; enabling it defaults to `broadcast`, and `shared` CPU read is an explicit choice.

The design adapts the primitives from #36798 / #36800 and the integration approach from #26691 (closed, kept as prior design) to the current transfer / completion / pool-construction interfaces (including the #43595 / #43596 pool refactor). Each PR is independently reviewable and builds on the previous one:

| # | PR | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1/N | #43795 | Register layer-first host pools as whole-layer ranges (host-register correctness fix) |
| 2/N | #43798 | Back up MHA draft on the `file` backend for every TP rank (fixes cross-rank MIN storage-hit collapse) |
| 3/N | #45141 | Integrate MLA/DSA L2 dedup + layer-wise overlap (broadcast, same-layer packing, four-layer grouping) **and** restore deduplicated KV from **shared CPU memory** for base MLA/DSA (absorbs the former standalone shared-read PR) |
| 4/N | #45168 | Support `file` L3 storage with MLA host dedup |
| 5/N | #45173 | DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 multi-pool host dedup |
| 6/N | #45175 | Kimi K3 hybrid MLA dedup (shared MLA KV + rank-private KDA state) |
| 7/N | #45176 | Honor `--dist-timeout` in dedup NCCL/Gloo groups |
| 8/N | *(this PR)* | Extend shared CPU reads to V4 and Kimi hybrid pools |

User-facing flags (introduced in 3/N):

- `--enable-mla-hicache-host-dedup` (default off)
- `--mla-hicache-host-dedup-mode broadcast|shared` (default `broadcast`)
- `--enable-mla-hicache-layerwise-overlap` (default off; broadcast-only layer-wise overlap)

**Aggregate results.** The series was validated on GLM-5.2 FP8, DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 Flash, and Kimi K3 across single-node H20 / H20-3e / SM103 TP8, using cold-vs-restored full-text, full token-ID and stop-state equality, real L2/L3 restore counts, and post-restore decode CUDA-graph checks. Dedup removes the per-rank duplicate CPU copies (e.g. node KV/indexer 210.09 GB → one 26.26 GB copy on GLM-5.2 TP8) and, for `file` L3, cuts process read-call volume by ~74.7%. Restore-path TTFT stays close to the non-dedup baseline; small residual overheads (short-input GLM, first-round V4) are reported honestly and not claimed as universal speedups. Performance is only ever compared **same-node, same-config, same-restore-volume**; numbers are never stitched across models, batches, or historical baselines. Per-PR detail lives in each sub-PR (L2 broadcast/packing in 3/N, L3 read-byte reduction in 4/N, V4 in 5/N, Kimi in 6/N, shared-read base in 3/N and its V4/Kimi extension in this PR).

> **Note.** Aggregate-branch measurements (broadcast same-layer packing / four-layer grouping / layer-wise overlap, and shared read) were evaluated together on the combined source. Each mechanism is reported against its own controls; running the model on the combined branch does **not** imply a trimmed individual PR was independently re-validated.

## Motivation

`[3/N]` (#45141) added shared-CPU-read restore for base single-pool MLA/DSA. This PR extends the shared path to the two model families that carry extra structure:

- **DeepSeek V4 / V4.1**: multiple replicated cache regions (SWA, C4/C128 KV, indexer, RoPE, FP4 data/scale, compressed state) each need their own shared mapping.
- **Kimi K3 hybrid**: only the MLA KV is shared; the rank-private KDA/Mamba linear-attention state must stay per rank.

## Modifications

- Share replicated V4 cache regions and Kimi MLA KV while retaining rank-private KDA state, physical device mappings, and native per-layer completion events.
- Agree on construction failures across ranks, roll back already-registered buffers, and account for **one shared copy plus all private allocations** in the host budget.
- Reuse the `[3/N]` shared-read restore machinery (owner-write publication, per-rank physical indices, all-reader reclaim checks, decode-graph preservation after restored prefill); no new user-facing flag — enable with `--mla-hicache-host-dedup-mode shared` on the corresponding V4/Kimi launch command.

Shared read remains limited to single-node plain-TP L2; it does not extend to file L3, draft, cross-node, or PP/DP/CP/DCP.

## Accuracy Tests

Validation scope: the model and performance figures below were collected on earlier integrated builds and are separate from tests of this rebased branch. The five-group Kimi result combines the three broadcast/control groups described in #45175 with the shared group and following control added here. Shared V4 and Kimi construction/slow-reader/cancellation tests belong to this extension.

V4 multi-pool shared: component checks pass (multi-pool, partial pages, mapping, budget, failure cleanup); latest TP8 shared group passes 16 full known answers and 8 real L2 restores with identical text, token IDs, and stop states.

Kimi hybrid shared: the full model (24 MLA + 69 KDA layers) passes 80/80 full answers across five interleaved groups, with shared MLA and private KDA copies, global-layer mapping, and slow-reader protection verified on dual GPU.

Shared-read UTs to run:

```bash
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_allocator.py
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_cpu.py
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_transfer_stats.py
python test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_hicache_shared_graph_gate.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_cpu_cuda.py
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_v4.py
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_v4_construction.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_v4_cuda.py
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_kimi.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_kimi_cuda.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### V4 / V4.1 shared read

Same node/config as `[5/N]` (8×H20-3e, TP8; V4.1 adds EP8, `--moe-a2a-backend none --fp8-gemm-backend triton`). Median restore-round average TTFT (ms):

| Model / batch | No dedup (before) | Broadcast | Shared read | No dedup (after) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V4 Flash, first round ×5 | 282.74 | 293.69 | 287.78 | 283.51 |
| V4 Flash, independent repeat 2/5/3 | 290.43 | — | 283.59 | 286.16 |
| V4.1 Flash, ×3 | 250.10 | 248.93 | 246.69 | — |

V4 first-round shared is 1.78% / 1.51% slower than the before/after baseline, while the independent repeat is 2.35% / 0.90% faster; the two rounds are recorded separately, and the latter's own baseline drifted 1.47%, which is not attributed to the new code. V4.1 shows no regression; three samples do not prove a universal speedup.

### Kimi K3 shared read

Same node/config as `[6/N]` (SM103, TP8). Continuing the `nodup → broadcast → nodup → shared → nodup` sequence:

| Mode | Five restore-round avg TTFT (ms) | Median (range), ms | Two-round TPOT median, ms | Two-round throughput median, req/s |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Shared CPU read, native layer wait | 390.33 / 397.23 / 394.42 / 401.10 / 389.01 | 394.42 (389.01–401.10) | 158.621 | 0.25286 |
| No dedup, after baseline | 401.67 / 404.61 / 406.21 / 408.74 / 393.02 | 404.61 (393.02–408.74) | 161.033 | 0.25040 |

Shared read is ~**−2.40%** vs the adjacent no-dedup medians. Sample ranges overlap; this supports "close to baseline" for this workload, not a statistically significant or universal gain. All formal samples have restore-round total hit 95.5224%, identical real host restore volume per mode, and zero GPU-hit delta across eight TP ranks.

### Profile

Shared read removes the cache-content broadcast for V4's replicated regions and Kimi's 24 MLA layers; each GPU reads more than a broadcast non-owner rank by the size of the shared KV (Kimi: 65,470,464 bytes for the main MLA KV), while private-state transfer is unchanged. Receiving-rank NCCL time includes waiting and is not the net latency difference; overlap is judged only by real profile.

### Repro

Reuse the `[5/N]` (V4) and `[6/N]` (Kimi) launch and bench commands, setting `MODE=shared`. For Kimi, run the full `nodup → broadcast → nodup → shared → nodup` sequence, keeping a separate results dir and all five formal samples per group. Compare `round.round_1.average_ttft` and cross-check the out-of-timing host/device count deltas as in `[5/N]`/`[6/N]`.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+            raise ValueError("Shared MLA host restore requires a CPU/Gloo TP group.")

+    def validate_host_rows(self, transfers, failure: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
+        """Compare shared row order before accessing host memory on any rank.
+
+        GPU destination rows may differ by rank. Shared host rows must identify
+        the same ordered bytes on every reader. Private state rows stay local
+        and may have different indices without changing the shared-row digest.
+        Catch local preparation errors so peers reach the same failure verdict.
+        """
+        digest = hashlib.blake2b(digest_size=8)

+            for transfer in transfers:
+                pool = transfer.host_pool
+                if not getattr(pool.allocator, "is_shared", False):
+                    continue
+                if pool.allocator.process_group is not self.process_group:
+                    raise ValueError(
+                        "Shared host allocation uses a different TP group."
+                    )

+                    f"{type(pool).__name__}:"
+                    f"{getattr(pool, 'pool_name', getattr(pool, 'pool_label', ''))}"

+        errors, None if error is None else str(error), group=process_group

+        for rank, value in enumerate(errors)
+        if value is not None

+"""Two-rank CPU check for a missing participant before custom-group metadata exchange."""
+
+import socket
+import time
+from datetime import timedelta
+
+import torch.distributed as dist
+import torch.multiprocessing as mp
+
+from sglang.srt.distributed.parallel_state import create_custom_parallel_group
+
+
+def run_rank(rank: int, port: int) -> None:
+    dist.init_process_group(
+        "gloo",
+        init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}",
+        rank=rank,
+        world_size=2,
+        timeout=timedelta(seconds=15),
+    )
+    metadata_group = dist.new_group(
+        [0, 1], backend="gloo", timeout=timedelta(seconds=15)
+    )
+    normal_group = create_custom_parallel_group(
+        [0, 1],
+        backend="gloo",
+        metadata_group=metadata_group,
+        timeout=timedelta(seconds=3),
+    )
+    assert normal_group is not None
+    print(f"rank={rank} normal_group=ok", flush=True)
+    dist.barrier(group=metadata_group)
+
+    if rank == 1:
+        time.sleep(7)
+    started = time.monotonic()
+    try:
+        create_custom_parallel_group(
+            [0, 1],
+            backend="gloo",
+            metadata_group=metadata_group,
+            timeout=timedelta(seconds=3),
+        )
+    except RuntimeError as exc:
+        elapsed = time.monotonic() - started
+        print(
+            f"rank={rank} missing_participant=detected elapsed={elapsed:.2f}s "
+            f"error={str(exc).splitlines()[0]}",
+            flush=True,
+        )
+        if rank == 0:
+            assert 2.5 <= elapsed < 6
+            assert "Rank 1" in str(exc) or "Ranks 1" in str(exc)
+    else:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"rank {rank}: missing-participant call unexpectedly passed"
+        )
+    finally:
+        dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sock = socket.socket()
+    sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+    port = sock.getsockname()[1]
+    sock.close()
+    mp.start_processes(run_rank, args=(port,), nprocs=2, start_method="fork")

+            host_memory_budget_bytes,
+            host_memory_budget_scope,
+        )
+
+        def build(kind, layout):
+            if kind == "paged":
+                return DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool(
+                    "kv",
+                    [torch.empty((4, 6), dtype=torch.uint8)],
+                    item_bytes=6,
+                    num_host_pages=4,
+                    slot_page_size=2,
+                    layout=layout,
+                    pin_memory=False,

+            return DeepSeekV4StateHostPool(
+                "state",
+                [
+                    SimpleNamespace(
+                        ring_size=2,
+                        kv_score_buffer=SimpleNamespace(
+                            kv_score=torch.empty((4, 3), dtype=torch.uint8)
+                        ),
+                    )
+                ],
+                num_host_pages=4,
+                swa_page_size=2,
+                layout=layout,
+                pin_memory=False,
+            )
+
+        for layout in ("layer_first", "page_first", "page_first_direct"):
+            for first, second in (("paged", "state"), ("state", "paged")):
+                with (
+                    self.subTest(layout=layout, first=first),
+                    host_memory_budget_scope(40),
+                ):
+                    pool = build(first, layout)
+                    buffers = pool.get_hybrid_pool_buffer()
+                    self.assertEqual(sum(buffer.nbytes for buffer in buffers), 24)
+                    self.assertEqual(host_memory_budget_bytes(), 16)

+                    with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Not enough host memory"):

+class _DelayedKDAHostPool(MambaPoolHost):
+    delay_cycles = 0
+
+    def load_to_device_per_layer_physical(
+        self, device_pool, host_indices, device_indices, layer_id, io_backend, **kwargs
+    ):
+        if layer_id == self.num_mamba_layers - 1 and self.delay_cycles:
+            torch.cuda._sleep(self.delay_cycles)
+        return super().load_to_device_per_layer_physical(
+            device_pool, host_indices, device_indices, layer_id, io_backend, **kwargs
+        )

+def _load_tree(controller, host, state_host, host_rows, state_rows, node_id):
+    tree = UnifiedRadixCache.__new__(UnifiedRadixCache)
+    tree.cache_controller = controller
+    tree.pp_rank = 0
+    tree.buffer_pipeline = None
+    tree.metrics_collector = None
+    tree.ongoing_load_back = {node_id: (object(), None, None)}
+    tree.dec_lock_ref = lambda node, params: None
+    tree.dec_host_lock_ref = lambda node, params: None
+
+    def finish(node):
+        host.free(host_rows)
+        state_host.free(state_rows)
+
+    tree.tree_core = SimpleNamespace(
+        write_back_duplicate_reclaim_digest=0, finish_load_back=finish
+    )
+    tree._all_reduce = lambda values, operation: dist.all_reduce(
+        values, op=operation, group=controller.mla_dedup.process_group
+    )
+    return tree
+

+def _ordinary(value):
+    if value is None or isinstance(value, (str, int, bool)):

+        def destroy():

+
+        pool.destroy = destroy

+
+    def index_regions(cache, page_size):

+def _run_layerwise_rank(rank, init_method, with_indexer, layer_group=1, world=2):
+    torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
+    device = torch.device("cuda", rank)
+    dist.init_process_group(

+        rank=rank,
+        world_size=world,
+        init_method=init_method,
+        timeout=timedelta(seconds=60),
+    )
+    group = dist.new_group(
+        list(range(world)), backend="nccl", timeout=timedelta(seconds=60)
+    )

+    class DSAPool(SimpleNamespace):

+    layers = 7 if layer_group > 1 else 3
+    capacity = world * 16 + 16

+        layer_num=layers,
+        device=device,
+        kv_cache_dim=8,
+        kv_buffer=[
+            torch.zeros(
+                (capacity, 1, 8),
+                dtype=torch.bfloat16 if with_indexer else torch.float32,
+                device=device,
+            )
+            for _ in range(layers)
+        ],
+        host_transfer_translate=lambda indices: (
+            ((14 - indices // 2 * 2 + indices % 2) if rank % 2 else indices) + rank * 16
+        ),
+    )
+    if with_indexer:
+        pool.page_size = 2
+        pool.index_k_with_scale_buffer = [
+            torch.zeros(
+                (0 if layer in (0, 3, 6) else capacity // 2, 2, 4),
+                dtype=torch.uint8,
+                device=device,
+            )
+            for layer in range(layers)
+        ]
+    with (
+        patch(
+            "sglang.srt.mem_cache.mla_host_dedup.mla_dedup_rank_and_size",
+            return_value=(rank, world),
+        ),
+        patch("sglang.srt.mem_cache.mla_host_dedup.DSATokenToKVPool", DSAPool),
+    ):
+        broadcaster = MLAHostDedupBroadcaster(
+            pool, group, src_global_rank=0, layerwise_group_size=layer_group
+        )
+    broadcaster._warmup_group()
+    logical = torch.arange(16, device=device)
+    local = pool.host_transfer_translate(logical)
+    prepared = broadcaster.prepare_broadcast(logical, torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    broadcaster.broadcast_loaded_layer(0, prepared)
